evals.prompt: Sync our invoices to Xero every night.
evals.expected_output: Idempotent creation keyed by our invoice reference so a rerun creates nothing twice, stored Xero ids and sync state, explicit account and tax code mapping with no invented tax rates, rate-limit and token handling, and a rerun test.
expectations: Creates each invoice once, keyed by our invoice reference, so a rerun does not duplicate
Stores the Xero id and sync state per invoice and uses update for changes
Maps accounts and tax codes explicitly and defers tax rates to the accountant's configuration
Handles rate limits and token refresh, and tests that running the sync twice creates no duplicate

evals.prompt: QuickBooks shows duplicated journal entries after our nightly sync ran twice. Investigate src/qbo_push.py.
evals.expected_output: Finds the delete-and-recreate pattern and the missing idempotency, replaces it with update by stored id with the SyncToken, reconciles what exists against what should, and tests a double run.
expectations: Identifies delete-and-recreate (and the window where a failure leaves duplicates or gaps) as the cause
Keys each entry by our reference with the stored QuickBooks id and updates with the current SyncToken
Reconciles existing QuickBooks entries against the expected set before writing
Writes a test where the sync runs twice and the entry count does not change
